title: Workflows and agents: who owns the control flow?

items.stem: What most clearly separates an agent from a workflow in a system built around a language model?

options.text: An agent calls a language model, while a workflow never uses one
In an agent the model chooses the steps; in a workflow code does
An agent can call tools like a calendar, while a workflow cannot
An agent suits harder tasks and so always gives better answers

items.stem: In a makerspace assistant, every time a student asks about a machine, our code searches the manuals, pastes the top three passages into a prompt, and makes one model call to write the answer. How should this design be described?

options.text: An agent, because it calls a model and also uses a search tool
An agent, because the model writes the final answer to the student
A workflow, because the model picks which search tool to use
A workflow, because our code fixes every step ahead of time

items.stem: The design in the previous item is changed: the model may now call search_manuals zero, one or several times, or call check_calendar, in whatever order it decides, before it answers. In one or two words, who now owns the control flow: the model or our code?

Design A is a fixed workflow that makes exactly 2 model calls for every request. Design B is an agent that makes 5 model calls per request on average. Assume every call costs the same. Over 500 requests, how many more model calls does B make than A, on average?
Which part of the makerspace assistant is the best candidate for an agent rather than a fixed workflow?

options.text: Open questions like "Can I make a 40 cm bracket this week, and on which machine?"
Booking confirmation: check the slot, save the booking, send the same email
Weekly reminder: look up tomorrow's bookings and message each student
Safety sign-off: check the training record, then allow or refuse the booking

items.stem: Which condition is the strongest reason to choose a fixed workflow over an agent for one task?

options.text: The task is important, so it deserves the most flexible design
The task uses tools, and only an agent is able to call tools
The steps and their order are known ahead and repeat each time
The task is simple enough that no language model is needed
